items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I was studying composition with Muhal... I was able to really study serious in-depth composition with Muhal Richard Abrams... When I met him he showed me new ways of doing things... From him I learned more about the history of jazz than anything else.

ctx.x: Yeah. At that point it’s like, now what am I going to do. I want to be a musician, I want to have a career in music. Did you have a particular goal in mind?

I don’t know, after I got through college I had met Fred Anderson and he had introduced me to Muhal Richard Abrams and Bunky Green and Rufus Reid. Because Rufus and Bunky happened to be going to school there working on their master’s degree I think at that time. And I had been offered positions by some corporations for computer work, I think IBM was one that offered me a position, and there was another one, I can’t think — if I can think of the company’s name I’ll tell you — they’d offered me a position. They…
Define fusion for me at that time.
